subject: Procurement path & exceptions — PO vs card / marketplace option
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Jill Turner <jill.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: procurement path & exceptions (post-demo)

Hi Jill —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we can align on commercial path:

1) Procurement preference: you mentioned Acme prefers PO for vendor spend. Can you confirm whether card payments are strictly disallowed for platform SaaS, or if cards are allowed up to a threshold?
2) Payment terms: do you require net30 invoicing, or does Acme require prepay for new vendors/pilot work?
3) Marketplace interest: you asked about buying through AWS Marketplace — would that simplify approvals on your side?

I attached an updated pricing worksheet (20260220-acme-pricing-v2.xlsx) and a short procurement checklist to show the typical items customers need (procurement-checklist.docx).

If PO is required, can you share the expected cadence (monthly PO vs annual contract + PO)? If cards are allowed, we can often start on a credit-card basis for pilots and convert to invoiced/PO later.

If there are any blockers (e.g., no PO allowed, strict prepay-only policy), flag them here and I’ll loop in our finance team to discuss an exception.

Proposed next step: if you can confirm the preferred commercial path by EOD Monday, I’ll put together the formal MSA/SOW and a mutual action plan.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: 20260220-acme-pricing-v2.xlsx, procurement-checklist.docx

From: Jill Turner <jill.turner@acme.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Corp Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: procurement path & exceptions (post-demo)

Ben —

Thanks for the recap and the materials. A few specifics from procurement:

- PO: Acme’s standard is to issue POs for contracted SaaS spend. Cards are *generally not* used for ongoing platform contracts above $5k/month.
- Terms: we do net30 for established vendors. For new vendors we sometimes require prepay for the first 1–2 months while we complete vendor onboarding and tax/W9 checks.
- Marketplace: buying through AWS Marketplace can help because it’s handled on a different legal/commercial track and often avoids PO for the buyer team — procurement still needs to approve the marketplace listing and terms.

Edge case: Our policy does not allow split payment methods (e.g., card for pilot + PO for conversion) unless legal signs off. If Redwood requires prepay or card-only for pilots, we’ll need an exception from our finance team.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can: 1) invoice net30 on PO, 2) accept a one-month prepay and then invoice net30, or 3) list on AWS Marketplace? Also we’ll need a vendor packet (W9, SOC 2 report, contact for security questionnaire).

Best,
Jill Turner
Vendor Manager — Acme Corp
procurment@acme.com

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Jill Turner <jill.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Feb 2026 08:43:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: procurement path & exceptions (post-demo)

Hi Jill —

Appreciate the detail. Quick answers and proposals:

- Invoice net30 on PO: yes, we support invoiced net30 once a PO is in place — we’ll need the PO number and billing contact to issue invoices.
- One-month prepay: we can accept a one-month prepayment as a transitional measure while onboarding is completed. That’s a finance-level approval but common for pilots.
- AWS Marketplace: we have a listing process in progress but not every region/offer is live. Marketplace purchase is a viable route and often simplifies buyer procurement, but timeline may add ~2–3 weeks to get the listing approved on Acme’s side.

Edge-case & exception handling: if Acme cannot do card and also cannot prepay, and insists on PO + net30 only, we can proceed but will need a signed MSA + PO to start. If Acme is open to a one-month prepay, we can start earlier. If a full PO is required but procurement needs vendor paperwork first, we can provide the vendor packet (W9, SOC 2 summary, contact for security questionnaire).

I’m copying Dylan (finance) to flag for a possible prepay waiver/exception if needed. Dylan — would you be able to authorize a single-month prepay option for ACME-2026-001 pending completed vendor onboarding?

Thanks —
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jill Turner <jill.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 09:10:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: procurement path & exceptions (post-demo)

Hi Jill —

Looping in on next steps. To help speed approvals on your side I attached a draft SOW (acme-sow-draft.pdf) and a one-page mutual action plan that maps deliverables, dates, and procurement steps.

What we typically need from Acme to start a pilot:
- Signed MSA (or PO referencing our MSA)
- PO number for invoicing
- Completed vendor form + W9
- Security questionnaire (we can complete your vendor risk assessment and provide SOC 2 Type II evidence and architecture notes)

If procurement needs an explicit ask for an exception (e.g., allow card for pilot or allow prepay), a short email from the hiring manager / budget owner to procurement usually helps speed the review. Happy to draft language for you if that’s helpful.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Attachments: acme-sow-draft.pdf

From: Jill Turner <jill.turner@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Corp Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 11:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: procurement path & exceptions (post-demo)

Thanks Marissa, Ben —

A few updates from procurement/legal:

- Legal requires the vendor risk assessment and SOC 2 Type II prior to any PO > $25k/year. Please send the SOC 2 report (or the SOC 2 auditor letter) and a short architecture/data flow diagram.
- We cannot do prepay as a permanent policy, but we can approve a one-time prepay for onboarding only with a written business justification and approval from our finance director.
- Regarding PO exemptions: procurement will consider a temporary exception for pilot purchases if the business leader signs off and provides a short justification explaining the time-to-value need. That approval must be routed through procurement and logged.

I’ll confirm internally whether Acme will pursue AWS Marketplace for this pilot or move forward with a PO + net30. If we need a template justification for the exception, please send and I can route it.

Best,
Jill

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Jill Turner <jill.turner@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 16:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: procurement path & exceptions (post-demo)

Thanks, Jill — super helpful. Recap and concrete next steps from our side:

1) I attached an updated pricing workbook that includes a one-month prepay option and the PO-invoicing path (20260220-acme-pricing-v2.xlsx).
2) I’ve asked Dylan in finance to prepare a short approval memo template that your business owner can use to request a temporary PO-exemption for the pilot (we’ll include justification language and estimated spend).
3) I’m attaching a vendor packet (W9 + SOC 2 summary) and our security contact info so your team can start the vendor risk assessment. If you need the full SOC 2 report we can share it under an NDA — happy to arrange.

Possible short-term workarounds if procurement needs time: purchase via AWS Marketplace (if your team can accept the listing) or a one-month prepay that we’ll credit back if you convert to a PO within 30 days. Dylan — any notes on how quickly finance can turn around the memo/exception?

We’ll stand by to support whichever path Acme prefers — happy to jump on a quick call with procurement/legal to move things forward.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: 20260220-acme-pricing-v2.xlsx, acme-sow-draft.pdf, procurement-checklist.docx
